what_happened: Task 784 (frozen-record tracker) lists task 769 among seven records that 'cannot be worked here and must not be dispatched' because their edit targets allegedly resolve only under the agent-system source store, implying this repo cannot reach it. On this machine the source store (/home/benjamin/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions/core) IS reachable and both target files (context/formats/plan-format.md, agents/planner-agent.md) were read directly and found byte-identical to this repo's deployed .claude/ copies despite the core extension being flagged stale overall. Proceeded with research as this dispatch's own instructions (source-store boundary resolution) explicitly direct, since this is a research-only phase (no edits). Flagging the apparent staleness/inaccuracy of task 784's frozen-record claim for whoever next touches that tracker or dispatches 769's implementation phase.

Research report drafted both provisions' exact prose and pinned both insertion points by verbatim surrounding text, so planning needed no re-derivation of wording or location; plan construction reduced to adopting the drafts, assigning tiers, and sequencing the deploy. Materially faster than a normal meta-task plan round.

The two provisions are logically independent and the dispatch says they can land in either order, but both edit the same file, so placing them in one wave would invite same-file concurrent edits under the wave model's parallelism promise. Serialized into separate waves (1 -> 2) and the reason stated in the plan's wave-table note. plan-format.md's wave model does not itself say what to do when two independent phases share one file.

Plan Phase 1's verify-deploy.sh invocation passed the core extension's own source-store directory as TARGET; the script requires TARGET to be the nvim config repo root (contains both agent-system/extensions/ and .claude/), so the as-written command errored with exit 2 (no deploy tree). Corrected to invoke with TARGET=/home/benjamin/.config/nvim; also ran generate-context-line-counts.sh --write there to clear a line-count mismatch gate-3 finding caused by the new 12-line paragraph (expected transient state until deploy regenerates it).

Phase 2 insertion landed clean on the first attempt with no deviation; reused the Phase 1 workaround (TARGET=/home/benjamin/.config/nvim, generate-context-line-counts.sh --write before the scoped gate) proactively, avoiding a repeat of the Phase 1 gate-3 transient failure.
